content.value_statement: Data teams need repeatable checks before analytics outputs become trusted. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design validation rules, dbt tests, and data contracts.
actual_capabilities: Explains completeness, uniqueness, validity, accuracy, consistency, and timeliness checks.
Provides Great Expectations setup patterns and expectation suite examples.
Shows dbt schema tests, custom generic tests, and singular tests.
Outlines data contract fields, ownership metadata, quality checks, and service levels.
Describes automated validation pipelines with reporting and failure handling.
limitations: Requires clear source tables, schemas, and business rules from the user.
Does not connect to warehouses or execute validations by itself.
Example thresholds must be adjusted for each dataset and operating model.
Sensitive validation outputs still need masking and access controls.

use_cases.title: Add Warehouse Tests
use_cases.description: Create dbt tests for fact and dimension models before release.

use_cases.title: Standardize Validation
use_cases.description: Build Great Expectations suites for critical tables and scheduled checks.

use_cases.title: Define Data Contracts
use_cases.description: Document schema rules, ownership, quality targets, and freshness expectations for shared datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Start Quality Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new dataset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a starter data quality plan for these tables: [tables]. Include completeness, uniqueness, validity, and freshness checks.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Expectations Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Great Expectations suite for [table]. Include checks for primary keys, required columns, allowed values, ranges, and freshness.

prompt_templates.title: Design dbt Test Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this dbt model context: [context]. Recommend schema tests, relationship tests, custom tests, and failure severity levels.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Contract Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a rollout plan for data contracts across [domains]. Include ownership, versioning, compatibility checks, alerts, and remediation steps.

output_examples.input: A team wants quality checks for orders, customers, and products.
output_examples.output: A validation plan with key checks, freshness targets, owners, alert routing, and release gates.

output_examples.input: A dbt model has missing customer links and late-arriving order records.
output_examples.output: Recommended relationship tests, recency checks, accepted thresholds, and triage steps for failed runs.

output_examples.input: A data product needs a contract before downstream teams consume it.
output_examples.output: A contract outline covering schema fields, PII notes, quality rules, service levels, owners, and change controls.

best_practices: Start with critical columns and user-facing datasets before adding broad coverage.
Separate warning checks from blocking checks, and define a fallback plan.
Mask sensitive values in validation reports, alerts, and shared artifacts.
anti_patterns: Copying sample thresholds without checking real data distributions.
Blocking production pipelines for low-impact warnings without escalation rules.
Publishing failed-row samples that expose personal or confidential data.

faq.question: Does this skill run Great Expectations or dbt?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and prompts that help an assistant design checks for your environment.

faq.question: Which tools does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Great Expectations, dbt tests, data contracts, and related quality pipeline patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with data contract design?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers schema fields, owners, quality rules, service levels, PII notes, and versioning.

faq.question: Is it useful without dbt?
faq.answer: Yes. The concepts also apply to Great Expectations, Soda checks, and custom validation workflows.

faq.question: How should teams choose blocking checks?
faq.answer: Use blocking checks for critical correctness issues, and keep warnings for non-critical quality signals.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Mask sensitive values in validation outputs, limit access to reports, and avoid sending raw samples to alerts.
